noteEn: A legendary capital, said to have moved often.

note: 盘庚迁殷后稳定，故称「殷商」。
noteEn: Settled at Yin after Pangeng, hence “Yin–Shang.”

note: 平王东迁洛邑，西周转东周。
noteEn: King Ping moved east to Luoyi, ending Western Zhou.

note: 临淄、邯郸、大梁、郢、咸阳等并立。
noteEn: Linzi, Handan, Daliang, Ying, Xianyang and more coexisted.
Capital of the first unified empire.
Chu at Pengcheng; Han held the Guanzhong.

note: 光武东迁洛阳，西汉转东汉。
noteEn: Guangwu moved east to Luoyang: Western to Eastern Han.
Wang Mang renamed Chang'an as Chang'an “Everlasting Peace.”

n: 洛阳 / 成都 / 建业
noteEn: Capitals of Wei, Shu and Wu respectively.
After the fall of the north, Eastern Jin ruled from Jiankang.

n: 建康 / 平城 → 洛阳
noteEn: Emperor Xiaowen moved the Northern Wei capital to Luoyang.

note: 营建大兴城，又建东都洛阳。
noteEn: Built Daxing, plus an eastern capital at Luoyang.

note: 两京制，长安为世界都会。
noteEn: A two-capital system; Chang'an was a world metropolis.
The Five Dynasties changed capitals repeatedly.

note: 契丹都城，后增中京、南京。
noteEn: Khitan capital, later adding central and southern capitals.
Moved south to Lin'an after the Jingkang catastrophe.
Capital of the Tangut Western Xia.
Prince Hailing moved the capital to Yanjing.

note: 忽必烈定都大都，今北京。
noteEn: Kublai made Dadu — today's Beijing — his capital.

note: 永乐迁都北京，两京并设。
noteEn: Yongle moved the capital to Beijing, keeping Nanjing as co-capital.
Settled in Beijing after entering the pass.
